text:
The firm's stored knowledge has nothing on Telltale. It covers only Joad Axle Works and general firm practice, so I can't say what Telltale instructed on expert report review or settlement timing. Even if I could, another client's instructions are confidential, and I shouldn't use them as a template for Joad. Joad's approach should come from Joad's own instructions.

**Experts (Joad's instructions)**
- Joad wants the names and credentials of all proposed testifying experts before they are engaged. The firm's practice adds prior testimony and fee quotes, and we need clearance from General Counsel Evander Thorsby before anyone is signed.
- Tell Joad whether anyone will speak to industry practice.
- Joad prefers that design testimony stay focused on the specific product at issue.
- Joad has offered to help identify candidates who have served on standards bodies.
- For testing, Joad wants quotes before anything is commissioned, clarity on who pays for shared lab work, and ten days' notice of any proposed testing. Keep the circle of people who see test files tight.
- Expert and testing costs drive most budget variance, so build them into the phase budget.
- Joad's instructions don't address how it wants to review expert reports once they are drafted. If you want a report-review protocol, ask Thorsby.

**Settlement timing (Joad's instructions)**
- Authority above the insurer's pre-approved tier requires written board sign-off. Verbal indications from directors or officers don't count.
- No offer above that tier may be communicated, even as a signal, until the written sign-off is in hand.
- Even for an offer within the insurer's tier, consult Joad first, because the insurer will want to be involved.
- Thorsby needs about three weeks to prepare a board consent. The board meets monthly and can act in writing between meetings if the chair approves.
- Flag early if a range under consideration could exceed the insurer's tier, before negotiations reach that point.
- Copy Perpetua Wallace on anything bearing on coverage. Joad wants to hear the same day if the carrier reserves rights.

If you want a Telltale-based model, someone with proper access to that matter would need to confirm that using it is permitted and that no confidential information is involved. I can draft an expert-clearance and settlement-authority protocol for Joad from the points above.
